Fett's flying ''Slave One''.|[[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], to [[Chewbacca]]|[[Star Wars (2020) 1|''Star Wars'' (2020) 1]]}} '''''Slave I''''', also spelled '''''Slave One''''' and also known as '''Boba Fett's starship''' and '''Jango Fett's starship''', was a modified [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray-31''-class patrol and attack craft]] used by the infamous [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett]] before the [[Clone Wars]] and later his unaltered [[Cloning|cloned]] son, [[Boba Fett]], just prior to the [[Republic Era|Fall of the Republic]] and during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire]]. The ship in its original form was produced by a subsidiary company of [[Kuat Drive Yards]], based on the [[planet]] [[Kuat]]. ==Description== ===Design and modifications=== {{Quote|A heavily modified ''Firespray-31''-class patrol craft, ''Slave I'' served Jango Fett for years before becoming the property of Aurra Sing, Hondo Ohnaka, and then Boba Fett. Jango outfitted ''Slave I'' with blaster cannons, concussion missiles, and seismic charges. Boba then added special modifications of his own. A powerful sensor jammer allowed ''Slave I'' to go undetected by most scanners, letting Boba Fett approach his bounties without being detected.|The ''Galactic Explorer's Guide''|''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]''}} [[File:BobaFettsStarshipAft-MF65.png|thumb|left|250px|''Slave I'' was highly modified by both Fetts.]] ''Slave I'' was a [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray-31''-class patrol and attack craft]] that was modified as far back as its [[time]] under [[Jango Fett]]. During this time, the only overt weapon systems leftover from its standard layout were the tail [[blaster cannon]]s, but he still made sure to upgrade them, allowing these [[cannon]]s to be fired with greater precision.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] Already during its time under Jango, ''Slave I'' was a very effective and customized [[Starship|ship]], armed with superior [[Deflector shield|shielding]] technology, high levels of endurance, and an arsenal of hidden and overt weapons. When his [[Reproduction|son]], [[Boba Fett]], took on the ship, he made his own modifications, so ''Slave I'' was filled with heavy-duty shield generators, several new weapons systems, and various types of auxiliary [[sensor]] systems. Additionally, a secret military sensor, which could be used for jamming and masking, allowed ''Slave I'' to disappear from the majority of scanning systems. The craft was equipped with overwhelming weaponry that could take out other heavily armed ships. However, with the exception of the twin blaster cannons, the weapons systems remained hidden to make the ship appear as if it was lightly armed. ===Interior=== Jango put ''Slave I'' through extensive modifications after several harsh battles in [[Realspace|space]]. Because the original fit of ''Firespray'' patrol craft was only furnished for short-term patrol runs, he added spartan crew quarters due to the long hunts he partook in. He also altered the previously police-regulation cages into coffin-like cabinets that were less-humane but better controlled his prisoners. By the ship's use under Boba, ''Slave I'' had what were described as "prisoner cages," which had six immobilizing bunks. In the [[cockpit]], sensor scopes displayed readouts for the starship's navigation, atmospheric data, and weapons systems. The interior of ''Slave I'' included a deck situated on a gyro system, allowing the occupants to stay upright no matter what position the ship was in. The ship also had a [[holoprojector]] in the main cabin as well as six chairs for passengers. The artificial [[gravity]] on each deck re-oriented, depending on the flight mode the ship was in. ==History== ===In the service of Jango Fett=== {{Quote|He must have put a homing device on our hull. Hang on, son. We'll move into the asteroid field, and we'll have a couple of surprises for him.|Jango Fett|}} [[File:Firespray_SotG.png|thumb|left|250px|''Slave I'' in orbit of Geonosis, under Jango Fett's ownership]] Jango Fett stole ''Slave I'' whilst undertaking a job on [[Oovo 4|Oovo IV]],{{BuildFalconCite|28|Starship Fact File}} a [[prison]] [[moon]] that ''Firespray'' attack craft were used to guard,''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' outfitting the craft with a number of weapons, including laser cannons, projectile launchers, and [[seismic charge]]s.{{Databank|boba-fetts-starship|''Slave I''}} While under Jango's ownership, the ship was used throughout his many adventures, including to rescue the criminal mastermind [[Phaedra]],[[Jedi Knights 4|''Jedi Knights'' 4]] throughout the search for the [[Hope of Glee Anselm]] statue,[[Jango Fett 1|''Jango Fett'' 1]] during the [[heist in the Outer Rim Territories]] and subsequent effort to bring his wounded friend [[Tarr Kligson]] to the [[Haven (droid outpost)|Haven]] [[space station]],[[Bounty Hunters 37|''Bounty Hunters'' 37]] to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Jango Fett)|travel]] to [[Ord Mantell]],[[Age of Republic - Jango Fett 1|''Age of Republic - Jango Fett'' 1]] and in a [[Dogfight over Geonosis|dogfight]] over [[Geonosis]] against a [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Jedi starfighter]] piloted by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. After Jango's death during the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], the craft came into the possession of his son, Boba, who used it throughout his failed quest to kill the [[Jedi Master]] who had beheaded his father, [[Mace Windu]]. Boba, his ally turned mentor [[Aurra Sing]], [[Castas]], and [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] traveled to the [[planet]] [[Florrum]] to meet with Sing's friend, [[spice]] [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] in the ship. After the arrival of the [[Jedi]] Master [[Plo Koon]] and [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], Fett and Bossk were captured. When Sing tried to escape on ''Slave I'', Tano leaped onto the ship's hull and sliced off a wing with her [[lightsaber]]. After this, Sing lost control of the ship and it crashed,{{TCW|Lethal Trackdown}} with the Jedi believing Sing to be dead. Ohnaka pulled her out of the crash site{{TCW|Assassin (episode)}} and took ownership of ''Slave I'' for a short period of time, before it returned to Fett's ownership near the end of the Clone Wars. ===Boba Fett's deadly craft=== {{Quote|You didn't just hurt my ship— you went ''inside?''''"
"''It was a ''tiny'' charge. Barely did any damage. Just wanted to shake you up a little.''"
"''Still… the ''disrespect.'' That vessel belonged to my father.|Boba Fett and Zuckuss|[[War of the Bounty Hunters 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 1]]}} [[File:BobaFettsStarship-MF65.png|thumb|250px|left|''Slave I'' was a feared side while under Boba Fett's ownership.]] The ship became well-known to [[the galaxy]]'s fugitives, who recognized it as the ship owned by one of the galaxy's deadliest bounty hunters. During the [[Imperial Era]], the ship was once repaired at the [[Imperial spaceport (Gall)|Gall Imperial spaceport]].''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the adult Boba flew ''Slave I'' to rendezvous with the [[Death Squadron|Imperial fleet]], where [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] tasked Boba and a group of bounty hunters to capture [[Han Solo]]. Boba tracked Solo and his ship, the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', to [[Cloud City]], landing the ''Slave I'' on the [[East Platform]]. After Solo's capture, Boba transported the [[Carbon-freezing|carbon-frozen]] rebel to bring him to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt's]] custody at his [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] on [[Tatooine]]. During Fett's journey, however, he became sidetracked upon learning about the return of [[Nakano Lash]],[[Bounty Hunters 1|''Bounty Hunters'' 1]] using ''Slave I'' during his search for his former ally to end his personal vendetta. After returning to his mission to bring Solo to Jabba, certain that Lash would die,[[Bounty Hunters 5|''Bounty Hunters'' 5]] Fett eventually took ''Slave I'' to the "[[smuggler]]'s [[moon]]" of [[Nar Shaddaa]], taking Solo to [[Doctor|Doc]] [[Ragon]] to ensure he would survive his carbonite imprisonment. Low on [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], Fett agreed to kill [[Fighting pit|pit]] warrior [[Wyrmen Lictor]] in exchange for the work, but, while Fett was away, Ragon was killed and Solo was taken[[War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha'' 1]] by agents of [[Crimson Dawn]].
[[File:PutCaptSoloInTheCargoHold-TESB.png|thumb|right|250px|Fett oversees Han Solo being loaded onto ''Slave I'' on Bespin.]]
After the new head of the organization, [[Qi'ra]], sent a message showing Solo to Jabba, the Hutt believed Fett had double crossed him and put a bounty on Fett. On Nar Shaddaa, ''Slave I'' was the site of trap launched by bounty hunters [[Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM]], yet Fett defeated them both. [[Robolobotomy|Hacking]] into 4-LOM's head, Fett used ''Slave I'' to return to Tatooine, where he learned Jabba was offworld and that Crimson Dawn had returned. During the [[Attack on the Executor|Attack on the ''Executor'']], Fett finally regained possession of Solo and traveled to Tatooine to receive his payment. He also had a [[carbon-freezing chamber]] installed on the ship in case Solo thawed again and used it against [[IG-88B]]. After defeating the [[assassin droid]],[[War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88'' 1]] Fett finally sold Solo to Jabba and received his payment.[[War of the Bounty Hunters 5|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 5]] [[File:AttackOnKintanStriders-BoBFCh4.png|thumb|left|250px|Fett attacks the Kintan Striders with the ''Slave I'']] After the war, with Fett believed dead at the [[Rescue of Han Solo|skirmish]] at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]], ''Slave I'' was kept in a [[Jabba's Palace garage|hanger]] at Jabba's Palace, now under the control of [[Bib Fortuna]]. Eventually, Fett and his new partner [[Fennec Shand]] infiltrated the palace and retrieved ''Slave I''. Fett then used the ship to track down and [[Attack on the Kintan Striders|destroy]] the [[Kintan Striders Gang|Kintan Striders]]. From there, Fett flew to the Pit of Carkoon with the hopes of finding his lost armor. As the ''Slave I'' descended into the pit, the [[sarlacc]] attacked them, latching onto the craft with its tentacles. Shand dropped a seismic charge into the sarlacc's maw, killing the creature and freeing the ship.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} Sometime later, Fett and Shand flew ''Slave I'' to the planet [[Tython]], where they had tracked the Mandalorian [[Din Djarin]] and his [[Force-sensitive]] [[foundling]], [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. After Grogu was [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|kidnapped]] by [[Phase-III Dark Trooper|dark troopers]] belonging to [[Moff]] [[Gideon]], Fett flew his ship into Tython's upper [[atmosphere]] to identify [[Gideon's light cruiser]]. With Djarin's [[Razor Crest|own ship]] destroyed and Fett now in Djarin's debt to help protect Grogu, Fett agreed to fly Djarin to [[Nevarro]] aboard ''Slave I'' as part of his plan to retrieve the child.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} [[File:KomrkSlaveIShuttle2743-TMCh16.png|thumb|right|250px|''Slave I'' docked next to Bo-Katan's ''Kom'rk''-class fighter and Shuttle 2743.]] Departing from Nevarro, Fett took Djarin and [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] to the [[Karthon Chop Fields]] to retrieve [[Migs Mayfeld]]. He then flew the party to [[Morak]], where Djarin and Mayfeld infiltrated an Imperial [[rhydonium]] refinery and Djarin accessed a computer terminal giving him the coordinates to Gideon's vessel. After the two men finished the mission, Fett rescued them from the roof of the refinery. As ''Slave I'' was flying away from the scene, it was targeted by two [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]]. Fett used a seismic charge to destroy the fighters. Following the Morak mission, ''Slave I'' was used to attack [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|Imperial shuttle]] [[Shuttle 2743|2743]] carrying [[Doctor|Dr.]] [[Penn Pershing]], a scientist working for Gideon. ''Slave I'' then transported Djarin to [[Lafete]] to recruit [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] and [[Koska Reeves]] in the [[Second rescue of Grogu|rescue]] of Grogu. After tracking down Gideon's cruiser and attacking the ship, Fett jumped into hyperspace per the group's plan. Sometime after the mission's success, Fett collected Shand and landed ''Slave I'' on Tatooine. There, the two [[Attack on Jabba's Palace (Boba Fett)|invaded]] Jabba the Hutt's former palace, killed [[Bib Fortuna]], and took over the remnants of Jabba's criminal empire.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} Fett had ''Slave I'' stored in the palace's hangar during his [[War against the Pykes|gang war]] with the [[Pyke Syndicate]]. ===Legacy=== [[Standard decade|Decade]]s later, the ''Slave I'' was mentioned in the ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'', a survival guide written by Hondo Ohnaka and [[DK-RA-43]]. It included a blueprint showing various features of the ship.''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' ==Behind the scenes== In the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'', ''Slave I'' was mistakenly named as ''Clone 1'' on two occasions. Since [[2021]],{{LEGOYouTube|video=GmxefUdQ00w|text=LEGO® CON 2021 - Full show - Live from LEGO House, Billund Denmark!}} ''Slave I'' has been referred to as "Boba Fett's starship" in official media, with this description appearing in merchandise,{{SW|url=news/hasbro-reveals-sdcc-2022|text=SDCC 2022: Hasbro Reveals New ''Mandalorian'', ''Star Wars Jedi: Survivor'' Figures and More}} individual works,''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' and reference material. The last media to use the ''Slave I'' name before''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' the widespread{{LEGOCite|num=75312|name=Boba Fett's Starship}}{{Databank|boba-fetts-starship|''Slave I''}} change was the book ''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' published on [[September 28]], [[2021]], although it has since been used in several [[Star Wars Day-at-a-Time Calendar|''Star Wars'' Day-at-a-Time Calendar]] releases.{{CalendarCite|24|''Slave I''|March 18}}{{CalendarCite|25|''Slave I''|June 11}}{{CalendarCite|26|''Slave I''|January 9}} In [[June]] [[2021]], a then-upcoming LEGO set of the ship set was renamed "Boba Fett's Starship", and the URL for the ship's entry on the official [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] was similarly changed,{{Databank|slave-i|''Slave I''|oldversion=20200210152459}} though the entry itself remained titled ''Slave I''.{{Databank|boba-fetts-starship|''Slave I''|oldversion=20210415055107}} On [[September 19]], [[2024]], the Databank entry was renamed to "Boba Fett's Starship" to match its URL, with no mention of the name ''Slave I''.
